dedupe_keys.name: buildingsbench buildings 900k synthetic load series and short term load forecasting benchmark

description: BuildingsBench is a dataset and benchmark for short-term load forecasting of buildings, published by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (now the National Laboratory of the Rockies) through the Open Energy Data Initiative, with Patrick Emami and Peter Graf as creators. Its pretraining set, Buildings-900K, holds synthetic energy consumption time series for about 900,000 residential and commercial buildings extracted from the End-Use Load Profiles database (the pretraining files are named for ComStock and ResStock runs with AMY2018 and TMY3 weather), one series per building, and is described as statistically representative of the US building stock. The benchmark adds seven real building consumption datasets for zero-shot forecasting and transfer learning: ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014, Building Data Genome Project-2, the Sceaux household power data, Borealis, SMART, IDEAL and Low Carbon London. Coverage: the United States building stock for the synthetic series; the evaluation sets come from several countries. Access: Parquet and CSV tar files on OEDI and its S3 data lake, with a pip-installable Python package providing PyTorch dataloaders, persistence to transformer baselines and metrics. Licence: the data is CC-BY-4.0 according to the OEDI submission page; the code is BSD-3-Clause; free. Caveats: the pretraining series are simulated, not metered, and the pretraining files are large. Simulation uses are training and testing building load forecasters that feed demand into grid and resilience models. Related records: the End-Use Load Profiles, ResStock and ComStock records.
